description: Implement the `random` native module providing pseudo-random number generation functions: random() -> float, randint(a, b) -> int, randrange(stop) -> int, randrange(start, stop) -> int, uniform(a, b) -> float, choice(xs) -> T for list[T] (or Any for dynamic lists), shuffle(xs) -> None for list[T], seed(n) -> None. Static types preferred but Any/dynamic accepted where applicable.
steps: Create directory random/ (Go package name `random`) with random.go containing const Name = "random" and func New() *module.NativeModule.
Implement random() - takes 0 args, returns float. Host function uses Go's math/rand/v2.
Implement randint(a, b) - takes 2 int args (or Any), returns int. Host function generates random int in [a, b] inclusive. When args are Any, return Any.
Implement randrange - 1 or 2 int args, returns int. randrange(stop) gives [0, stop), randrange(start, stop) gives [start, stop). Accept dynamic args returning int.
Implement uniform(a, b) - takes 2 float args (or Any), returns float.
Implement choice(xs) - takes list[T], returns T. For dynamic list or Any, returns Any. Host function picks random index.
Implement shuffle(xs) - takes list[T], returns None. Host function shuffles in place.
Implement seed(n) - takes int, returns None. Host function seeds the RNG.
Create random/random_test.go testing New() returns expected symbols and result type validation.

Add compiler integration tests in compiler/random_test.go: verify types are correct and programs compile/run without error. Test `import random
x: int = random.randint(1, 10)
print(str(x))` compiles and runs. Test `from random import random
y: float = random()
print(str(y))` compiles and runs.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./compiler passes with random integration tests
A minipy program `import random\nx: int = random.randint(1, 10)\nprint(str(x))` compiles and runs
